column1: # TITLE: Gene Expression of HBEC-3KT cells exposed to cigarette smoke condensate (CSC) over a period of 15 months

# SUMMARY: We define how chronic cigarette smoke-induced time-dependent epigenetic alterations can sensitize human bronchial epithelial cells (HBEC) for transformation by a single oncogene. The smoke-induced
column2: chromatin changes include initial repressive polycomb marking of genes later manifesting abnormal DNA methylation by 10 months. At this time
column3: cells manifest epithelial to mesenchymal changes
column4: anchorage-independent growth and upregulated RAS/MAPK signaling with silencing of hyper-methylated genes normally inhibiting these pathways and which are associated with smoking related NSCLC. These cells
column5: in the absence of any driver gene mutations
column6: now transform by introducing a single KRAS mutation and form adeno-squamous lung carcinomas in mice. Thus
column7: epigenetic abnormalities may prime for changing oncogene senescence to addiction for a single key oncogene involved in lung cancer initiation.
